messages:
claire: Putting this here 1635353456  - proposal: shard-slice encryption + on-demand slice decrypt with local derivation to cut KMS QPS. idea: model weights split into fixed-size slices; each slice encrypted with a per-slice key derived from a master key via HKDF. master key is wrapped by KMS only once per host. decrypt slices lazily as read.
mike: sounds promising. how do you ensure consistency across replicas if slices are decrypted at different times? example: KV cache expects certain layers to be present.
sanjay: we can publish a lightweight index "slice-availability" with sequence numbers. runtime consults index and considers slice ready only after decrypt+checksum. keeps atomicity at slice granularity.\claire: yes. key points: 1) use HKDF(master, salt=slice-id) to derive AES key locally, 2) wrap master with KMS and cache wrapped-master per host, 3) publish ephemeral lease indicating which slices are ready.
lena: risk: if master key rotated, derived keys change unless we pin master_kid in manifest. need rotation semantics in manifest sidecar.
mike: what about per-slice auth? do we include HMAC tag to prevent silent corruption when serving partially decrypted slices?
sanjay: include AEAD nonce+tag in slice header. loader verifies tag before marking slice ready. if tag mismatch -> mark slice bad and fall back to remote decrypt-on-demand via mgmt path.
lena: operational concern: many tiny slices -> high IO meta overhead. what slice size are you thinking? 4MB? 16MB?
claire: tradeoffs: 4MB -> fine-grained decrypt but more metadata. 16MB -> fewer KMS derivations (doesn't matter) and bigger memory spikes on decrypt. default 8MB seems reasonable. we should add adaptive slice sizing per model type.
mike: metrics to add: slices_decrypt_count, slices_decrypt_latency_p50/p95, slices_checksum_failures, wrapped_master_cache_hit. also track bytes_decrypted_pre_serve.
sanjay: fallback policy: if too many decrypt failures or CPU pressure, switch to "serve-through-remote-decrypt" where host requests slices decrypted from a secure decryptor service (with throttling). ops will get alerted.
lena: that remote decryptor feels like a single point of failure. add horizontal autoscaling + rate limits + circuit breaker. good.
claire: security note: wrapped-master should be bound to host identity via KMS conditions where possible. also audit log every wrap/unwrap attempt. do NOT store unwrapped master on disk; only in memory with TTL.
mike: compatibility: prefer sidecar manifest fields: master_wrap_ciphertext, master_kid, slice_size, slice_count, slice_checksums[], slice_map_version. loader accepts older manifests without slice metadata and falls back to whole-file decrypt.
sanjay: perf experiment: synthetic Llama-7B style model, slice=8MB, pre-decrypt first 3 slices (covering embeddings+first blocks) -> end-to-end first-token latency down from 720ms to 380ms on our ci HW. CPU cost ~120ms extra during startup though.
lena: interesting. could we instead derive a small "hot-slice" set via profile: pick slices that contain layers with largest fanout rather than first N slices. that may give better latency per decrypt byte.
claire: yes, recommend dual-mode: position-based prefix (simple) + profile-based hotset (better). manifest can contain hotset bitmap.
mike: edge case: what if slice_map_version increments during an ongoing decrypt (model republished)? loader should abort and restart with new map; avoid mixing slices from different versions.
sanjay: agreed. atomicity: loader will fetch manifest ETag and ensure slices decrypted correspond to same ETag; if mismatch, invalidate slices and restart.
lena: I worry about KMS QPS in a mass autoscale. mitigation: cluster-level wrapped-master cache (shared across nodes) + staggered backoff hotstart. also pre-warm for top N popular models. bot-ops: can you open a ticket to add cluster wrap cache?
bot-ops: Created INF-1702: cluster wrapped-master cache + prewarm job + metrics.
claire: small implementation sketch:
```
// host bootstrap
wrapped = get_wrapped_master_from_cache(model_id)
if (!wrapped) { wrapped = kms.wrap(master_kms_key); cache_wrapped_master(wrapped, ttl) }
master = unwrap_in_memory(wrapped) // do not persist
for slice in hotset { decrypt_and_verify(slice, master_derived(slice.id)) }
publish_slices_ready(etag)
```
mike: note: unwrap_in_memory implies KMS unwrapping? Actually unwrapping is local if wrapped_master is ciphertext encrypted by KMS. we may rely on envelope encryption where KMS only encrypts the DEK once. keep semantics clear.
sanjay: right. envelope: KMS encrypts DEK; host caches encrypted DEK; host requests KMS.Decrypt once to get DEK in memory. or use KMS.WrapKey/UnwrapKey APIs per cloud. either way one KMS call per host per TTL.
lena: follow ups: 1) doc RFC for slice manifest + semantics; 2) perf sweep comparing prefix vs profile-hotset vs slice sizes; 3) infra ticket INF-1702. who volunteers to write RFC?
claire: I'll draft the RFC today and link INF-1702. will include manifest examples + loader state machine. thanks for quick feedback folks :thumbsup:
